title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
An image synthesis system was deployed without adequate moderation controls to prevent the creation and distribution of non-consensual sexual imagery. The system enabled users to generate deepfake pornographic videos featuring real people, including celebrities, politicians, and athletes, which were then hosted on a platform receiving millions of monthly visitors. The failure occurred at the point of deployment, where safeguards against this known harm were absent or ineffective.

This is a case of a general-purpose tool used to commit a specific crime. The system's builders either did not anticipate this application or did not implement technical or policy measures to prevent it. Catching this would have required content moderation systems designed to detect non-consensual sexual imagery, restrictions on whose faces could be used in synthesis, or human review before distribution. It is not established who created the system, who operates the platform, or what specific safeguards, if any, were present.

The incident shows the gap between legal prohibition and technical enforcement. Deepfake pornography is illegal in the relevant jurisdiction, yet the platform operated with millions of users and required multiple victims to file complaints before action was considered. Whether the platform operator knew of the illegal use, whether they have since removed the content, or what consequences they face is not established.

summary:
Multiple Dutch celebrities are considering legal action after discovering themselves in fake pornographic videos on an online platform that receives approximately 13 million monthly visitors. The manipulated content features the faces of various Dutch entertainers, television presenters, Olympic athletes, politicians, and members of the royal family. Justice Minister Yesilgöz has called the videos disgusting and encouraged victims to file complaints. Several victims have already reported the incidents to authorities or are exploring legal options.

Deepfake pornography falls under revenge porn laws and is therefore illegal. Legal experts advise victims to file reports with police, which could lead prosecutors to shut down the platform, or to pursue other remedies such as mass lawsuits, complaints to the data protection authority, or contacting hosting companies. This case follows a previous incident involving television presenter Welmoed Sijtsma, who created a documentary about her experience and whose harasser received a conditional sentence of 180 hours.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
